sections.heading: C — Hazardous and aggressive driving
sections.markdown:
## C — Hazardous and aggressive driving

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A27
Sharp bends, slick pavement and pooled water all order slower speeds, since rubber meets road only through tire grip. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]
FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A27
Keep tires sound and aired per the owner book, and crawl gravel and dirt where stops stretch and turns skid. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]
FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A27
Shed speed before curves because mid bend braking breaks traction and sends cars sliding. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]
FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A27
Dead intersection signals legally become stop signs for every approaching driver. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]
FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A27
First rain, snow or sleet means ease off: drop ten miles per hour wet, halve speed on packed snow with snow tires or chains, and crawl ice or skip driving it. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]
FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A27
Studded tires stay legal in Connecticut from November fifteenth through April thirtieth. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]
FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A27
Suspect ice in shady hollows, on uninsulated bridges, near freezing wetness, and during first minutes of hot day rain lifting asphalt oil. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]
FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A27
Wet tires grip only to about thirty five miles per hour before skimming water, sooner when bald, and downpours can float them fully, so slow down. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]
FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A27
Once floating, lift off the gas, steer straight with only slow emergency turns, and brake or steer solely after grip returns. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]
FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A27
Aggressive driving can ripen unknowingly into road rage with deadly fallout, so privilege demands self control behind the wheel. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]
FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A27
Rage feeds on jams, angry parent models, fading courtesy, and green youths rattled by tense moments. [A27]
Source: [A27 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0027]
FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A28
Rage also feeds on life stress spillover, claimed road territory, false armor feelings at speed, and cars mistaken for body extensions. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]
FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A28
Defuse by phoning police later not punishing now, refusing races, venting to riders, delaying angry trips or handing keys over, and granting blunderers the doubt of fatigue. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]
FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A28
Trouble brews from lane blocking, tailgating that sparks deadly fights, unsignaled cuts with stuck blinkers, rude fingers, and horn abuse including green light blasts. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]
FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A28
Trouble also brews from red light lane squatting, sloppy parking and handicap theft with door dings, high beam wars solved by dimming plus night four second gaps, merge hogging, trailer blocking and chatty road stands, and endless alarms. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]
FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A28
Deny hostile drivers eye contact and acknowledgment, and when chased flee to police posts or bright public stores, never home. [A28]
Source: [A28 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0028]
